intro: Six scenes, one week: how to run the paper system.
outro: The kick-off grid is what they said. The open sheet is what they owe. The notebook is what happened.

monday.lead: Monday, six fifty-five. The week is already printed.
steps: Take the pack from Sunday: one open sheet, five dated grids.
Write the week's three targets, each with a date.
Put the fixed points in today's three. That is your calendar.
Stop at ten minutes.
monday.lands: Targets on the open sheet. Appointments in today's three.

ptw.lead: Seven twenty. Khang says the FIR permit is still not issued.
steps: One line on today's grid, beside his name.
Before the walkdown, one row on the open sheet. You set the date.
On the power-up path? Add the flag, and circle the date.
ptw.lands: The grid is what he said. The sheet is what he owes.

idea.lead: Ten forty. An idea arrives in the corridor.
steps: Write it on the back page of the notebook. Dated, one line.
It does not touch the open sheet.
On Friday it dies, becomes a dated action, or joins the roadmap.
idea.lands: No date, no owner. So it waits.

target.lead: One ten. The third target moves.
steps: Strike through the old target. Do not reword it quietly.
Write the new outcome beside it, with the date and the reason.
One line on the notebook: the decision, and who took it.
Update the rows that depended on that date.
target.lands: The sheet keeps both versions. Friday explains itself.

three.lead: Four thirty. Three lines, not an essay.
steps: Done, moved, blocked. One line each, on the notebook.
Tomorrow's appointments into tomorrow's today's three.
Send the nudges due today, before the laptop closes.
three.lands: Three lines now. A report on Friday.

friday.lead: Friday, one o'clock. Thierry at two.
steps: Tick what closed. Mark what did not. Read the struck targets.
Three lines from the week: done, blocked, risk.
Assemble the report. Fifteen minutes.
Then close the laptop. The meeting is not a reconstruction.
friday.lands: The report is a by-product, not an excavation.
